concept.name: Seed phrase
concept.definition: A seed phrase (recovery phrase) is a human-readable list of typically 12 or 24 words that encodes the entropy from which all of a wallet's private keys are deterministically derived, serving as the master backup for the wallet.
concept.intuition: It is the master key written in words: anyone who reads it owns everything the wallet controls, forever.
concept.mechanics: Wallets following standards such as BIP-39 generate the phrase from random entropy and derive the entire key hierarchy from it, so re-entering the phrase on any compatible wallet regenerates the same accounts. Wallet providers instruct users to write it down offline because it is the only recovery path.
concept.failure_modes: Phishing attacks that ask users to 'verify' their seed phrase are the dominant wallet-drain vector; storing it in cloud notes, photos or email makes remote theft trivial, and losing it makes funds unrecoverable.
concept.misconceptions: A seed phrase cannot be changed after the fact — if it leaks, the only remedy is moving funds to accounts derived from a new phrase. The wallet app's password does not protect a leaked phrase.
concept.example: A 12-word phrase like 'there aeroplane curve vent formation doge possible product distinct under spirit lamp' can regenerate every account in the wallet on a new device; whoever types it into any wallet software gains full control of the funds.
